# DEdata

> What data engineering job postings in Germany ask for: tools, German-language requirements, cities and advertised salaries. Counted every morning from two public job APIs. Open source; every figure traces to a committed daily snapshot.

Figures from the run of 12 November 2026, tracked daily since 11 September 2026. Every percentage is a share of the 334 currently advertised postings that carried a description to read.

## German-language requirement

Only an explicit competency phrase counts as requiring German, and most German postings are written in German regardless, so the German shares are floors, not ceilings.

- All postings: 41.3% (138 of 334) state a German requirement; 30.2% (101 of 334) mention English without requiring German
- Bundesagentur für Arbeit: 44.0% (133 of 302) state a German requirement; 26.5% (80 of 302) mention English without requiring German
- Arbeitnow: 15.6% (5 of 32) state a German requirement; 65.6% (21 of 32) mention English without requiring German

## Median advertised salary by tool

Advertised, not paid. Only a minority of postings state a salary, tools with fewer than three that do are left out, and n is the number of postings each median is taken over.

## Method

- Sources: the Bundesagentur für Arbeit's public job API and the Arbeitnow board. Nothing is scraped.
- Scope: data engineering, analytics engineering, BI and data analyst roles, entered only where Germany is established by the source or resolved from the location text. Unknown stays out.
- Deduplication: postings are collapsed on employer and title, which merges an employer's genuinely different roles under one title.
- Freshness: a posting counts while the sources are still listing it, for 7 days after it was last seen.
- Each run is a fresh sample of that morning. Read a one-day change as noise.
